hook.text: Your rival trips on stage and you feel a flash of delight. Schadenfreude—joy at another's misfortune—is universal.

buildup.text: The German word has no English equivalent, but the emotion appears in every culture studied. We all feel it.

discovery.text: Brain scans show schadenfreude activates the ventral striatum—the same reward center as food and sex.

twist.text: Schadenfreude is strongest toward people we envy. The higher someone's status, the more their fall pleases us.

climax.text: It serves a social function: it enforces norms. When rule-breakers suffer, the group feels satisfaction and cohesion.

punchline.text: We enjoy others' falls because fairness demands it.
